answer: Split control from ownership: a key signs 2-of-3, shares held by three unrelated custodians, each capped at M clients and bonded per client. A custodian alone sees who funds a key, so noticing batch sign-ups is its job. Two clients from one funding source at one custodian forfeits its bond and freezes all clients six epochs, a tenth to the whistleblower. A thousand keys then need five hundred bonded firms liable for strangers; one bad batch costs a decade of fees, so silence stops paying. Basalt cracks into columns as it cools; an island yields nectar only where the rock has already split.
